question: For decoder-only Transformers with additive residual streams and linear OV and unembedding interfaces, does linear decodability force semantic information into a context-invariant subspace, can an isolated class token identify that subspace without labeled examples, and do modular-arithmetic, head-level classification, and sparse-autoencoder results establish architectural necessity rather than merely empirical linear accessibility?

key_findings.claim: The Invariant Subspace Necessity theorem is much weaker than the paper's architectural-necessity framing because its definition of a communicable feature already assumes the relevant scalar is linearly decodable.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 3.4 assumes that a linear functional of a linear interface recovers g(f(c)). Theorem 3.7 then sets w_f = W-transpose phi and observes that contexts requiring the same scalar output differ in w_f-perpendicular. This proves agreement on one projection, but it does not by itself show that the model's full semantic representation is low-dimensional, unique, context-independent in any stronger sense, or aligned with a token representation.

anchors.section: 3.2 Formal Definitions and 3.3 Main Theoretical Results

key_findings.claim: The appendix constructs an invariant subspace by spanning all chosen feature-relevant components, making existence largely tautological and leaving the claimed unique decomposition under-specified.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix A.1 requires w_f-transpose h_f(c) to equal the output and eta(c) to lie in w_f-perpendicular, then calls the decomposition unique. Unless h_f is additionally constrained to span(w_f), an arbitrary w_f-perpendicular vector can be shifted between h_f and eta. Defining S_f as the span of the resulting h_f(c) ensures a context-aggregated span exists, but does not establish the nontrivial invariant geometry advertised in the main text.

key_findings.claim: The capacity argument does not prove that vocabulary pressure forces semantic feature factorization.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 3.8 and Appendix B.1 note that |V| is much larger than d, introduce an informal dimensional-plus-interference cost, assume sparse feature co-occurrence and shared semantic attributes, and declare a shared-factor solution optimal. No optimization objective, weighting of the two costs, alternative distributed code, or theorem connecting trained Transformer parameters to the proposed optimum is specified; dimensional shortage forces non-orthogonality, not uniquely semantic factors.

anchors.section: Appendix B.1 Detailed Proof of Proposition 3.8

key_findings.claim: The claimed K-minus-one dimensional bound does not justify directional invariance for the full feature representation.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix A.2 asserts that K linearly separable representative embeddings must be affinely independent, then notes that K centered representatives span at most K-minus-one dimensions and transfers this upper bound to the minimal invariant subspace. The affine-hull fact about selected representatives neither requires affine independence nor bounds all within-class feature-relevant variation. Appendix B.3 merely restates the proposition without repairing that logical gap.

anchors.section: Appendix A.2 Proof of Proposition B.2

key_findings.claim: The exact Self-Reference theorem weakens to an approximation in its full proof.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.13 states h_t is proportional to d_ft. Appendix B.4 instead derives h_t = lambda_t d_ft + eta_t with an unconstrained orthogonal component and says proportionality holds only approximately when a token primarily expresses one dominant feature. The later Apple experiment explicitly relies on a token carrying multiple superposed meanings, so exact token-as-direction identity is not generally established.

anchors.section: 5.3 Polysemy as the inverse of Partial Synonyms

key_findings.claim: The nonlinear-head modular-division experiment shows that a nonlinear readout can coexist with non-Fourier, non-linearly-probeable hidden states, but it does not show that a linear head necessarily produces the claimed semantic geometry.
key_findings.evidence: A two-layer Transformer with an MLP classification head on modular division modulo 97 reaches about 95% validation accuracy while a detached linear probe reaches about 20% and PCA lacks a circle. Some random seeds nevertheless develop Fourier structure and then the probe succeeds. The paper does not report the number of seeds, uncertainty, training configuration, or a matched linear-unembedding control in this experiment.

key_findings.claim: Class-token and same-class instance vectors align more often than different-class vectors in four LLaMA-3-8B datasets, but the prose overstates the plotted range.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 gives head-above-diagonal rates of 91.5% for Countries, 97.6% for Animals, 86.0% for Cartoon Characters, and 89.6% for Emotions. The following paragraph instead says 89.6%-98.6%, excluding the 86.0% result and introducing an unplotted 98.6% maximum.

key_findings.claim: The class-token probes often classify implicit prompts well in larger models, but the table reports the single best attention head and does not support a uniform-method claim.
key_findings.evidence: For LLaMA-3-8B, unsupervised best-head accuracy ranges from 53.52% on Emotions to 94.32% on Animals, while zero-shot ranges from 52.43% to 89.12% and SAE from 38.32% to 93.92%. The unsupervised method loses to zero-shot on Countries (79.60% versus 82.97%) and Languages (87.80% versus 89.12%), contradicting the prose that it consistently outperforms zero-shot classification.

key_findings.claim: GPT-2-Small is a substantial negative result for broad claims that all three geometric methods achieve strong classification.
key_findings.evidence: Its best-head SAE, unsupervised, and zero-shot accuracies are only 15.73%, 21.76%, and 20.11% for Authors; 20.21%, 28.14%, and 20.83% for Cartoon Characters; and 17.69%, 21.32%, and 17.37% for Emotions. Languages is the exception at 84.02%-88.11%. Several results are close to plausible class-frequency baselines, whose exact values cannot be fixed because the paper gives inconsistent class counts.

key_findings.claim: Dataset definitions and denominators conflict between the main table and the appendix.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 specifies six Emotional Sentences classes with 60 instances each and six Literary Quotes classes with 50 instances each. Appendix D.1 lists seven emotion labels and says 600 examples were sampled, while listing seven authors with only 20 quotes per author. Table 1 also labels the literary task differently from Table 2, which calls it Authors. These discrepancies prevent reconstruction of chance rates and sample counts.

key_findings.claim: The best-head protocol provides an optimistic descriptive upper envelope rather than an unbiased estimate of generalization.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 explicitly selects the single best-performing attention head for every model, method, and dataset, but the paper gives no held-out head-selection split, multiple-comparison correction, confidence interval, or independent repetition. Supervised probes are omitted for alleged overfitting without reporting those results or applying the same selection audit to the retained methods.

key_findings.claim: The SAE evidence shows overlap between token and instance latents, but no null model establishes that the overlap is surprising.
key_findings.evidence: At top-k equal to 32, the paper reports shared token/instance dimensions of 15 for mammals, 23 for fish, 25 for reptiles, and 22 for birds. It provides no latent-dictionary size in the result, expected random intersection, permutation test, comparison with frequency-matched tokens, or uncertainty. Appendix D supplies additional visualizations but no quantitative null analysis.

anchors.section: Figure 4 and 5.4 Tokens Predict Feature Activation in SAEs
5.4 Tokens Predict Feature Activation in SAEs

key_findings.claim: The Apple polysemy experiment is compatible with superposition but does not isolate the claimed magnitude-only contextual modulation.
key_findings.evidence: Combining Fruits and Companies yields 69.0% accuracy with one Apple token and 65.7% with separate 'Fruit apple' and 'Company Apple' tokens. Both are treated as confirmation, even though the distinct-token condition is worse and there is no baseline that manipulates direction selection versus magnitude while controlling tokenization and prompt semantics.

anchors.section: 5.3 Polysemy as the inverse of Partial Synonyms

key_findings.claim: The held-out-month appendix is qualitative evidence rather than a measured zero-shot result.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 6 shows PCA and t-SNE plots after training the unsupervised transformation on odd months and calls the even-month clusters tight around prototypes. No classification accuracy, chance baseline, sample count, uncertainty, or comparison to the untransformed representation is reported on the page.

key_findings.claim: LayerNorm preserves a transformed direction only conditionally, not unconditionally.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B.2 requires d_f not lie in the all-ones span and positive input standard deviation, then maps the direction to gamma elementwise-multiplied by the mean-centered d_f. It does not assume that the learned gamma leaves this transformed direction nonzero, and the feature coefficient is rescaled by a context-dependent 1/sigma(h(c)).

anchors.section: Appendix B.2 LayerNorm Preserves Directional Invariance

key_findings.claim: The attention result preserves a feature direction only through the OV map after conditioning on attention weights; it does not extend architectural necessity through nonlinear routing.
key_findings.evidence: Corollary B.3 decomposes the output into an attention-weighted magnitude multiplying W_O W_V d_f. The QK circuit determines those weights through content-dependent dot products and softmax. The authors accordingly list nonlinear QK routing as outside the main guarantee, so the theorem cannot explain every feature used by a Transformer.

key_findings.claim: No causal experiment verifies that the token-derived directions are the mechanisms used by the model rather than correlates accessible to a probe.
key_findings.evidence: The empirical studies classify head outputs and compare SAE activations, while Corollary B.4 only algebraically states how adding a direction shifts linear-unembedding logits. The paper does not intervene on token directions, ablate them, compare causal effects to learned directions, or test whether preserving the projection preserves task behavior.

anchors.section: Appendix B.5 Corollary B.4 Distributional Influence

method.core_idea: Define semantic communication through a linear Transformer interface, turn the resulting readout functional into a putatively invariant feature subspace, hypothesize that an isolated token supplies its feature direction, and test token-instance geometry with head-level zero-shot, token-only trained, and sparse-autoencoder classifiers.
method.mechanism: A context c maps to a hidden state h(c). A feature is declared communicable when multiple contexts share it and some linear functional phi-transpose W h(c) recovers a scalar function of its value. Theorem 3.7 rewrites this as w_f-transpose h(c), identifies w_f-perpendicular as irrelevant to that scalar, and defines an invariant span of feature-relevant components. An informal capacity argument says a vocabulary much larger than the residual dimension favors sparse shared feature factors. Under an additional one-dimensional assumption, h(c) is decomposed into a context-varying magnitude along d_f plus orthogonal residual information. The Self-Reference Property then treats a class token's isolated hidden state as an estimate of d_f. Experiments compare an MLP output head on modular division, cosine alignment of class tokens with implicit instances, projection onto mean-centered class-token vectors, a linear transformation trained contrastively on class tokens only, and per-head TopK sparse autoencoders trained on instance activations. Classification reports the best attention head across eight constructed or reused datasets and four model families; appendices supply theorem proofs, LayerNorm/OV corollaries, one held-out-month visualization, SAE plots, and dataset descriptions.
assumptions: The feature of interest is already recoverable through a scalar linear functional of the selected interface; this is built into communicability rather than derived from architecture.
Agreement of a readout projection across same-feature contexts identifies the model's semantic representation rather than only a sufficient decision statistic.
A feature-relevant component and its span are uniquely defined independently of arbitrary orthogonal decompositions.
Vocabulary dimensional pressure, sparse co-occurrence, and shared attributes optimize a semantic factorization rather than another distributed or superposed code.
K class representatives bound the dimension of all feature-relevant within-class variation.
The relevant subspace collapses to a single direction and orthogonal components do not carry the same feature through another path.
An isolated token canonically and predominantly expresses the same feature used by diverse contextual descriptions.
Tokenization, polysemy, lexical frequency, morphology, and shared superclass semantics do not dominate token-instance cosine similarity.
Euclidean cosine and projection are meaningful without the causal inner product or whitening emphasized by prior linear-representation work.
Individual attention-head outputs inherit the theorem's interface-level guarantee even though they are intermediate branch outputs rather than final residual or unembedding states.
Selecting the best head on the reported examples estimates generalization rather than search over many noisy probes.
SAE top-k latent overlap indicates a common semantic direction rather than base-rate activation frequency or correlated training data.
The constructed prompt datasets are independent of pretraining memorization and have consistent class definitions.
A nonlinear-head negative control isolates the effect of the output interface despite changing the trained objective parameterization and omitting a matched linear-head run.
LayerNorm gain parameters do not annihilate the mean-centered feature direction, and nonlinear QK routing can be treated separately from feature communication.

techniques.role: Composes a semantic output functional with OV or unembedding weights to obtain a residual-space readout vector.
Groups contexts with equal required outputs and observes that their hidden-state differences lie in the readout null space.
Uses vocabulary-versus-hidden-dimension pressure and sparse co-occurrence to motivate shared feature factors.
Projects an instance activation onto a normalized token-derived class direction.
Uses an isolated class token or short class prompt as its own zero-shot semantic prototype.
Learns a linear orthogonalizing transformation from class-token prototypes without instance labels.
Trains a sparse autoencoder on each attention-head output and compares token and instance activations in the latent dictionary.
Replaces linear unembedding with an MLP classifier on modular division and separately measures Fourier structure and linear probe accuracy.
Compares one shared Apple prototype with domain-qualified prototypes across fruit and company descriptions.
Tracks a direction through mean centering, scalar normalization, and learned elementwise gains under explicit conditions.
Separates attention-weighted feature magnitude from the fixed linear transformation of its value direction.

evaluations.setting: Modular division modulo 97 with a two-layer Transformer and MLP classification head (p. 3, Figure 2; p. 4, Section 3.6)
evaluations.metric: Validation accuracy of the nonlinear head, detached linear-probe accuracy, and qualitative Fourier/PCA geometry
evaluations.result: One reported non-Fourier run reaches about 95% with the MLP head while its linear probe reaches about 20%; some unspecified random seeds instead develop Fourier structure and linearly probe well
evaluations.baseline: No matched standard linear-unembedding training result, seed count, error bar, or full training configuration is reported

evaluations.setting: LLaMA-3-8B class-token versus implicit-instance alignment (p. 5, Section 3.8 and Figure 3)
evaluations.metric: Percentage of attention heads whose class token has greater cosine similarity to same-class than other-class mean instances
evaluations.result: Countries 91.5%, Animals 97.6%, Cartoon Characters 86.0%, and Emotions 89.6%
evaluations.baseline: The prose reports a conflicting 89.6%-98.6% range; no random-token, frequency-matched, shuffled-label, or confidence baseline is given

evaluations.setting: Eight best-head classification tasks in LLaMA-3-8B (p. 7, Table 2)
evaluations.metric: Top-1 accuracy of SAE, token-only unsupervised, zero-shot identity-projection, and conditional-log-likelihood text-output methods
evaluations.result: Unsupervised accuracy spans 53.52%-94.32% and is below zero-shot on Countries (79.60% versus 82.97%) and Languages (87.80% versus 89.12%); SAE spans 38.32%-93.92%
evaluations.baseline: Text output spans 42.00%-99.67%; chance rates are not reported, and only the single best attention head is retained

evaluations.setting: Cross-model best-head comparison in LLaMA-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, and GPT-2-Small (p. 7, Table 2)
evaluations.metric: Top-1 task accuracy for SAE, token-only unsupervised, zero-shot, and text-output methods
evaluations.result: Larger models are often strong, but GPT-2-Small reaches only 15.73%-21.76% on Authors across the three geometric methods and 17.37%-21.32% on Emotions, while Languages is 83.37%-88.11%
evaluations.baseline: The text-output GPT-2 baselines are 12.50% on Authors, 49.80% on Emotions, and 15.67% on Languages; inconsistent class counts prevent a reliable chance comparison

evaluations.setting: Dataset coverage and denominator audit (p. 6, Section 5.1 and Table 1; p. 19, Appendix D.1)
evaluations.metric: Number of classes and instances per class
evaluations.result: Table 1 says six emotion classes times 60 and six literary classes times 50, whereas Appendix D.1 lists seven emotions with 600 sampled examples and seven authors with 20 quotes each
evaluations.baseline: No released split ledger or reconciliation is provided in the pinned paper

evaluations.setting: Combined Fruits and Companies polysemy test (p. 7, Section 5.3; p. 8, Figure 5)
evaluations.result: A single Apple prototype reaches 69.0%; separate 'Fruit apple' and 'Company Apple' prototypes reach 65.7%
evaluations.baseline: No non-Apple, tokenization-controlled, shuffled-prototype, or direction-versus-magnitude intervention is reported

evaluations.setting: Animal-class SAE shared-latent analysis (p. 7, Figure 4; p. 8, Section 5.4)
evaluations.metric: Intersection of the token's top-32 SAE dimensions and the most frequent instance dimensions
evaluations.result: Mammals share 15/32, fish 23/32, reptiles 25/32, and birds 22/32 dimensions
evaluations.baseline: No expected overlap under the dictionary width, random-token control, permutation test, or uncertainty interval is reported

evaluations.setting: Odd-month training and held-out even-month visualization (p. 16, Appendix C.1 and Figure 6)
evaluations.metric: Qualitative PCA and t-SNE proximity of held-out months to class prototypes
evaluations.result: The authors describe held-out even-month clusters as tight around their prototypes
evaluations.baseline: No held-out accuracy, chance level, sample count, untransformed embedding, or numeric cluster metric is supplied

evaluations.setting: Invariant Subspace Necessity proof audit (p. 11, Appendix A.1)
evaluations.metric: Whether the assumptions imply a unique, nontrivial context-invariant semantic subspace
evaluations.result: The proof establishes a common scalar projection and constructs a span over chosen feature-relevant components; its claimed decomposition is not unique without an additional parallel-to-w_f constraint
evaluations.baseline: A trivial full residual space or the one-dimensional readout span always satisfies weaker variants, so architectural necessity requires a stronger minimality or causal statement

evaluations.setting: Directional-dimension proof audit (p. 11, Appendix A.2; p. 14, Appendix B.3)
evaluations.metric: Logical support for dim(S_f) at most K-minus-one and one-dimensional binary features
evaluations.result: The proof bounds the affine hull of K selected representatives but does not bound all feature-relevant variation, and Appendix B.3 only restates the claim
evaluations.baseline: Prior categorical-representation work gives explicit causal and geometric conditions for simplex or polytope structure rather than inferring it from representative count alone

evaluations.setting: LayerNorm and OV transport analysis (pp. 13-15, Appendix B.2 and B.5)
evaluations.metric: Conditions under which a feature direction remains linearly decodable through normalization and attention output
evaluations.result: Mean centering and fixed gains map d_f to gamma elementwise times its centered direction, while OV maps it to W_O W_V d_f; magnitudes remain context-dependent
evaluations.baseline: The guarantees exclude an all-ones direction, require nonzero variance and a non-annihilating gain map, and do not cover nonlinear QK routing

limitations: Author-stated: the theory covers features communicated through linear interfaces; features used through nonlinear gating such as QK routing may not exhibit the claimed invariance.
Author-stated: the paper does not characterize when a higher-dimensional invariant subspace collapses to a single direction.

Overclaim audit (reviewer-inferred): defining communicability by linear decodability and then proving existence of a compatible linear projection does not establish that Transformers are broadly 'interpretable by design.'

Internal-contradiction audit (reviewer-identified): Theorem 3.13 states exact proportionality between a token and its feature direction, whereas Appendix B.4 retains an orthogonal residual and only claims an approximation for predominantly single-feature tokens.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix A.1 calls the h_f-plus-eta decomposition unique without constraining h_f to the readout span, leaving arbitrary orthogonal shifts possible.
Reviewer-identified: the capacity-factorization proposition has no formal optimization problem and does not rule out nonsemantic distributed encodings.
Reviewer-identified: the K-minus-one dimension proof reasons from selected class representatives to an entire feature subspace without a valid bridge.

Negative/conditional result (author-reported, reviewer-emphasized): some nonlinear-head modular-division seeds develop Fourier geometry, so the nonlinear interface permits both linear and nonlinear solutions; the number and distribution of seeds are absent.

Reviewer-identified: the modular experiment omits the matched linear-head control needed to test the stated architectural contrast and gives no architecture, optimizer, dataset size, seed count, or uncertainty details.
Internal-contradiction audit (reviewer-identified): Figure 3 contains an 86.0% head-alignment result, while the prose claims all four datasets lie between 89.6% and 98.6%.

Negative-result audit (reviewer-identified from Table 2): GPT-2-Small is near plausible chance on several class tasks, contradicting the blanket description that all methods achieve strong classification.
Internal-contradiction audit (reviewer-identified): main-table and appendix class counts and instances disagree for Emotions and Literary Authors, preventing reproducible chance baselines.
Reviewer-identified: reporting only the best head after searching every head can substantially inflate accuracy, and no held-out head-selection split or correction is described.

Reviewer-identified: the token-only 'unsupervised' probe uses named class tokens and a contrastive class identity objective, so it is label-free at the instance level but not free of semantic class supervision.
Reviewer-identified: class-token tokenization, multi-token prompts, lexical frequency, casing, and choice of layer/position are not documented sufficiently to reproduce the prototypes.
Reviewer-identified: SAE training details, dictionary widths, random-overlap baselines, and independent runs are absent from the pinned paper.

Reviewer-identified: public phrases, Goodreads quotations, and hand-compiled descriptions may overlap pretraining data, so prototype classification does not isolate compositional semantic generalization.
Reviewer-identified: Euclidean cosine is assumed even though the closest formal predecessor shows that geometry depends on a causal inner product.
Reviewer-identified: results on the best individual attention-head output are not directly licensed by a theorem about a feature decoded through a model-level linear interface.
Reviewer-identified: no causal ablation or steering experiment demonstrates that token-aligned directions are necessary or sufficient mechanisms for the classified behavior.
Reviewer-identified: the held-out-month appendix supplies only dimension-reduced plots and no quantitative held-out evaluation.
Reviewer-identified: the paper provides no code or data link in the pinned arXiv record, and several datasets are only informally described.
failure_modes: A feature decoded only after nonlinear routing, gating, or an MLP can remain inaccessible to the proposed linear interface argument.
A linearly accessible decision statistic can be mistaken for the model's full causal representation of a concept.
Arbitrary orthogonal components can make token and context states nonparallel even when their readout scalar agrees exactly.
Polysemous, relational, continuous, cyclic, or hierarchical concepts can require multiple directions or a curved manifold rather than one token vector.
Subword tokenization and multi-token class names can make an isolated token a poor or nonexistent canonical feature expression.
Mean-centering across a small class set can remove shared semantic content or manufacture contrastive directions dependent on which other classes were chosen.
Euclidean cosine can rank directions differently from a covariance-aware or causal metric, changing both head selection and classification.
Best-head selection can fit noise or dataset artifacts when hundreds of heads are screened on the same examples.
A frequent SAE latent can create large token-instance top-k overlap without representing the intended class.
Constructed descriptions can be memorized or lexically cue the answer, inflating apparent context invariance.
A learned token-only transform can overfit the geometry of known class labels and fail on unseen semantic families.
LayerNorm can annihilate or distort a direction when its centered component or gain-weighted image is zero or small.
QK routing can make whether a direction is communicated depend sharply on context even when the OV transformation itself is linear.
Dataset denominator errors can make chance comparisons and cross-model conclusions irreproducible.
A nonlinear output head can still learn a linear solution, so a single non-Fourier run cannot identify interface causality.
Intervening along a correlated token direction may shift logits while bypassing or damaging the actual computation that produces the feature.
reusable_insights: Separate the weak claim of linear accessibility from the strong claim that a model causally represents a concept as a unique direction.
A linear decoder always identifies a task-relevant quotient of representation space: states differing in the decoder null space are observationally equivalent to that readout.
Negative controls that alter output-head expressivity can test whether a representation is forced, but they require matched architectures, seeds, and training protocols.
A named token can be a useful zero-shot prototype even when no theorem makes it the unique semantic direction.
Prototype mean-centering removes common class components and can improve discrimination without instance labels.
SAE token-instance overlap should be calibrated against dictionary width, activation frequency, random tokens, and permutations.
For attention, distinguish the fixed linear transformation of value content from the nonlinear, context-dependent decision about where that content is routed.
Claims about invariant geometry should report within-class variation and cross-context transport, not only class-centroid alignment.
Multidimensional or manifold-valued features are a direct falsifier for universal one-token/one-direction accounts.
Best-component reporting needs a nested selection/evaluation split whenever many heads, neurons, or SAE latents are searched.
open_questions: Can Theorem 3.7 be reformulated as a non-tautological minimal or causal subspace result without defining the feature as linearly decodable in advance?
What additional constraint makes the feature-relevant decomposition unique, and is that constraint satisfied by trained Transformer states?
Can a formal objective prove that vocabulary pressure selects semantic factorization over arbitrary distributed codes?
Under what conditions does a K-valued feature's entire within-class variation lie in a K-minus-one dimensional subspace?
Do isolated token directions remain optimal after whitening or using the causal inner product from Park et al.?
How do single-token, multi-token, polysemous, and relational class expressions differ as zero-shot prototypes?
Does intervention or ablation along the token-derived component causally change the intended feature while preserving unrelated capabilities?
How much best-head accuracy survives nested head selection, independent test prompts, and correction for multiple comparisons?
Do the reported results replicate with reconciled datasets, released prompts, fixed splits, multiple seeds, and confidence intervals?
Is SAE token-instance overlap larger than frequency-matched and random-prototype null distributions?
Can the method detect and represent irreducibly multidimensional or curved semantic features rather than forcing a one-direction classifier?
Does the proposed invariance persist across layers, positions, paraphrase families, languages, and adversarially misleading contexts?
What happens when QK routing rather than OV/unembedding is the only path by which the downstream computation uses a feature?
Can a matched linear-versus-MLP readout experiment across many modular tasks quantify how often each head forces or merely encourages probeable geometry?

competitive_landscape.title: On the Origins of Linear Representations in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Jiang et al. derive linear concept representations from a latent next-token model, log-odds constraints, and gradient-descent implicit bias, with explicit ambiguous subspaces and simulations. The target presents architecture as a complementary cause, but its core result assumes linear decodability and does not supply comparably identifying conditions.

competitive_landscape.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. already formalize linear representations in output and input spaces, connect them to probing and steering, and derive a causal non-Euclidean inner product from counterfactual pairs. The target substitutes a single isolated class token for counterfactual pairs and uses Euclidean projection, while claiming an architectural explanation.

competitive_landscape.title: The Geometry of Categorical and Hierarchical Concepts in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. extend the linear-representation formalism to feature vectors, categorical polytopes and simplices, and hierarchical orthogonality, validating more than 900 WordNet concepts in Gemma and LLaMA-3. The target's K-minus-one and class-token claims overlap this territory but use best-head prototype classification and a weaker dimension argument.

competitive_landscape.title: Not All Language Model Features Are One-Dimensionally Linear
competitive_landscape.difference: Engels et al. rigorously define irreducible multidimensional features, discover circular day/month features through SAEs, and causally intervene on those subspaces in Mistral-7B and LLaMA-3-8B. The target allows higher-dimensional subspaces in name but empirically treats class features as single directions and supplies no causal intervention.

competitive_landscape.title: The Origins of Representation Manifolds in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Modell et al. explain how continuous, multidimensional feature values can form representation manifolds and relate intrinsic feature distance to on-manifold geometry, with text-embedding and token-activation tests. The target instead posits fixed invariant subspaces and offers a particularly simple token prototype for discrete classes.

competitive_landscape.title: Truth-value judgment in language models: ‘truth directions’ are context sensitive
competitive_landscape.difference: Schouten et al. directly test context effects on truth-direction probes and find sensitivity to logically relevant and irrelevant context, varying by layer, model, and data, with causal interventions. This is concrete negative evidence against interpreting every linearly probeable feature direction as context invariant.

competitive_landscape.title: The Lattice Representation Hypothesis of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Xiong combines linear attribute directions, separating thresholds, Formal Concept Analysis, and half-space intersections into a concept-lattice account with WordNet experiments. It addresses hierarchy and logical composition rather than why a single token should reveal a direction, but further narrows broad claims to originate architectural concept geometry.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first principled architectural explanation that linear Transformer interfaces necessarily create context-invariant semantic subspaces, plus a Self-Reference Property under which an isolated token directly identifies its feature direction and unifies zero-shot probes with SAEs.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper supplies a linear-functional theorem and appendices, an informal vocabulary-capacity factorization argument, a nonlinear-readout modular-division control, token-instance head alignment, eight best-head classification tasks across four model families, token-only contrastive probes, SAE latent overlap, and conditional LayerNorm/OV corollaries.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The broad theory claim is not established: communicability already assumes linear decodability, the proof constructs a compatible span rather than identifying a unique low-dimensional causal representation, the dimensional argument is incomplete, and exact self-reference becomes approximate in the appendix. Earlier work already formalizes output/input-space directions, probing, steering, categorical polytopes, multidimensional SAE features, and representation manifolds, with stronger causal or geometric conditions. The narrow contribution that plausibly remains is a simple single-token prototype heuristic, its token-only orthogonalizing probe, the particular MLP-head negative-control intuition, and descriptive evidence that token prototypes sometimes align with instance and SAE features. Those are useful empirical observations, not proof that linear interpretability universally works by architectural necessity.

reviewer_notes: The complete indexed 19-page arXiv v1 extraction was read end to end, including the full proofs in Appendices A-B, held-out-month visualization in Appendix C, all supplementary SAE figures, and Appendix D.1 dataset descriptions. The PDF and extracted-text hashes were independently recomputed and match the full-text index. Findings labeled author-reported reproduce the paper's statements; contradiction-audit and reviewer-inference entries distinguish proof/evaluation audits from author conclusions. Current primary records were checked on 2026-08-23 for seven close competitors. Full arXiv HTML/PDF content was inspected for Jiang v1, Park v2, categorical/hierarchical geometry v3, and multidimensional-feature v3, rather than relying on title similarity; current records for representation manifolds, context-sensitive truth directions, and the ICLR 2026 lattice hypothesis were also opened. Confidence is high in page-level transcription and the logical locations of the gaps, but lower in any claim about the intended unpublished implementation because the pinned paper does not expose code, split files, complete modular-training settings, or reconciled dataset counts.
